sources.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou — Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path
sources.locator: §6 opening Lemmas 6.1–6.2; §6.1 Lemma 6.4 and proof; entire §6.2 Lemma 6.5 and Claims 6.5.1–6.5.3, Figure 9

contents.name: 6.2 Bird graph
contents.support: Correct the introductory Bird-free typo to co-Bird-free, as in Lemma 6.5.

contents.name: Claim 6.5.1(1), proof and Figure 9 — The edge-plus-isolate co-Bird obstruction
contents.support: In a co-Bird-free graph, x,y outside H are nonadjacent and complete to an induced H=P2+P1. No outside u in N(x) minus N(y) is mixed on the edge and anticomplete to the isolate.

contents.name: Claim 6.5.1(2), proof and Figure 9 — The path-plus-isolate co-Bird obstruction
contents.support: Under the same complete nonedge-pair hypotheses, H=P3+P1 cannot have u adjacent to its isolate and two consecutive path vertices but not the third.

contents.name: Claim 6.5.2 proof, paragraph beginning Therefore — A mixed vertex on E is pure on both terminal edges
contents.support: For a co-Bird-free graph with nonadjacent x,y complete to E, an outside u in N(x) minus N(y) mixed on its underlying P5 is pure on p1p2 and p4p5.

contents.name: Claim 6.5.2, whole proof — Complete nonedge pairs force purity on induced E graphs
contents.support: Under the two-complete-nonadjacent-vertices hypothesis, every outside u in N(x) minus N(y) is pure to E. In a special-vertex comb, each vertex in another block is pure to every E copy in B_i.

contents.name: Lemma 6.5 proof after Claim 6.5.2, definitions of X,Y,R — E overlap chains inside one comb block
contents.locator: Lemma 6.5 proof after Claim 6.5.2, definitions of X,Y,R
contents.support: Let X be all vertices lying in an induced E in B_i and Y=B_i minus X. On X relate d,d-prime when there is a finite vertex chain from d to d-prime with consecutive vertices lying in a common induced E in B_i; allow length-zero chains.

contents.name: Lemma 6.5 proof, R equivalence and E anti-connected paragraph — E overlap classes form an anticonnected partition
contents.locator: Lemma 6.5 proof, R equivalence and E anti-connected paragraph
contents.support: The E-overlap relation is an equivalence relation. If X is nonempty its classes partition X into nonempty anticonnected sets; each E copy belongs to one class.

contents.name: Claim 6.5.3 base case and last contradiction — Purity propagates through E overlap chains
contents.locator: Claim 6.5.3 base case and last contradiction
contents.support: An external vertex pure to every induced E in B_i is pure to every E-overlap class.

contents.name: Lemma 6.5 proof, construction of L1 and Ls — The E overlap blockade and mixed quotient sequence
contents.locator: Lemma 6.5 proof, construction of L1 and Ls
contents.support: For nonempty X order its equivalence classes to form L1; recursively put L(s+1)=L(s)/M, using the established mixed-reachability quotient.

contents.name: Lemma 6.5 proof, finite termination paragraph — E overlap quotients terminate at a pure blockade
contents.support: For nonempty X the E-overlap quotient sequence reaches a pure blockade in at most |L1|-1 strict mergers; every stage has anticonnected blocks and coarsens L1.

contents.name: Claim 6.5.3 proof, nonedge paragraph — A separated anticonnected block pair forbids mixing in one direction
contents.support: In a co-Bird-free graph let D1,D2 be disjoint nonempty sets with D2 anticonnected; distinct outside x,y,z satisfy xy nonedge, x,y complete to D1 union D2, zx edge, zy nonedge, z complete to D1 and anticomplete to D2. No vertex of D1 mixes on D2.

contents.name: Claim 6.5.3, entire induction and descending witness proof — External purity survives every E overlap quotient
contents.locator: Claim 6.5.3, entire induction and descending witness proof
contents.support: In a co-Bird-free special-vertex comb, every vertex of another comb block is pure to every block at every stage of the E-overlap quotient sequence.

contents.name: Lemma 6.5 proof, paragraph proving (2.2) — The terminal E overlap pattern is E-free
contents.support: The pattern of the terminal pure E-overlap quotient has no induced E.

contents.name: Lemma 6.5(1),(2.1)–(2.3), complete proof; singleton convention adjustment — A special-vertex co-Bird-free comb admits an E-free structural partition
contents.locator: Lemma 6.5(1),(2.1)–(2.3), complete proof; singleton convention adjustment
contents.support: For each block B_i of a comb in a co-Bird-free graph with outside v complete to all blocks and anticomplete to all teeth, there is B_i=X_i disjoint union Y_i with Y_i E-free and X_i partitioned into a nonempty pure blockade with E-free pattern, every block of which is pure to each individual vertex of every other comb block.

contents.name: Figure 9, first witness — The first co-Bird witness by adjacency
contents.support: Use vertex order (x,y,u,a,b,c) and edges xa,xb,xc,ya,yb,yc,xu,ua,ab.

contents.name: Figure 9, second witness — The second co-Bird witness by adjacency
contents.support: Use vertex order (y,u,a,b,c,d) and edges ya,yb,yc,yd,ub,uc,ud,ab,bc.

contents.name: Claim 6.5.2 proof, finite neighbourhood case expansion — All E neighbourhood patterns under a complete nonedge pair
contents.locator: Claim 6.5.2 proof, finite neighbourhood case expansion
contents.support: On E with ordered vertices p1,p2,p3,p4,p5,q, the 64 possible external adjacency subsets reduce to the empty and full subsets after excluding the two Claim 6.5.1 patterns.

contents.name: Lemma 6.5, empty-overlap convention boundary case — The no-E-copy boundary case of the comb partition
contents.support: Take vertices a,b,v and edges ab,vb. The one-tooth comb (a,{b}) with special vertex v has no E; choose X={b},Y=empty and the one-block partition.

sources.title: Diestel — Graph Theory, sixth edition, Chapter 1: The Basics
sources.locator: §1.1 pp.2–4 complete; §1.4 pp.10–11 opening through component paragraph after Proposition 1.4.1 only

contents.name: 1.1 Graphs
contents.support: Use finite simple graphs, isomorphisms, induced subgraphs and complements to check both six-vertex witnesses. Graph unions, deletion, complete/independent sets and line graph terminology also occur; the line graph definition is not used.

contents.name: 1.4 Connectivity
contents.locator: p.10 opening through component paragraph on p.11
contents.support: Connected means nonempty with a path between every pair; apply in complements and concatenate paths through shared vertices.

contents.name: Proposition 1.4.1
contents.locator: pp.10–11, statement and complete induction proof
contents.support: The connected-prefix vertex-order argument independently explains the successive joining of connected sets, used here in the complement.

contents.name: Components (unnumbered definition and partition observation)
contents.support: Components are maximal connected induced subgraphs; distinguish these from E-overlap classes, which are only asserted to be anticonnected, not maximal anticomponents.

contents.name: Line graph (unnumbered definition)
contents.reason: The proof uses complements and induced subgraphs on vertices; it never replaces edges by vertices, so the line-graph construction has no role in this comb partition.
